title: Apple to consider Chinese NAND chipmaker: report
text:
9:49 a.m. ET Share 
By Emily Bary 
Apple Inc. AAPL, +1.84% may start buying NAND flash memory chips from a state-backed Chinese company, according to the Nikkei Asian Review , which wrote Wednesday that the two companies had been in talks. Were Apple to indeed bring on the company, Yanktze Memory Technologies, as a supplier, it would mark the first time the smartphone maker bought memory chips from a Chinese company, according to the report. Apple currently gets NAND chips from several providers, including Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd. 005930, +3.07% Toshiba Corp. 6502, +1.92% and Western Digital Corp. WDC, +0.43% the Nikkei Asian Review said, and the company might only start out with a small order from Yangtze if a deal is reached. Memory chips have become expensive over the last two years and Apple has already made a move to own part of a distributor . Shares of memory companies including Micron Technology Inc. MU, +1.92% and Western Digital were down in Wednesday morning trading. Apple's stock is down 0.5% in Wednesday trading but up 22% over the past 12 months, compared with a 20% rise for the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, +1.03% Quote References
